meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, Hale, and before or after hearing him?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now show me what you have on the essay.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:52, 11:58. He drafts elsewhere and pastes it in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Then hear this, Hale. Whatever happens next, nothing goes on his record and none of it reaches his class.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Then he got the scene wrong. Students misattribute lines all the time.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then what are you proposing, Hale? Whatever it is stays private.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Outlines change. That's what they're for.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine, to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Tonight, in writing, with nothing on his record spelled out. And the rewrite happens before December 1, as you said.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
He works most afternoons; I'll check tonight. Put Thursday in the email, and who supervises.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal

Hale,

Today you agreed to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's Hamlet essay under procedure 4.4, after school, not in front of his class and before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require all of that in writing, along with the Thursday date and the name of whoever will supervise. I expect it tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite before December 1 under 4.4. She still wants your written confirmation tonight that nothing goes on his record, with Thursday and the supervisor named. That is the fair outcome, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her pasting defence by asking for a dated draft, because it was specific and she could check it herself.
What cost ground: Nothing lost you ground, though the outline came while she was waiting for your proposal and added nothing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on a late October night, very close to what she saw. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what you were proposing after the misquoted line stood, offer 4.4 right then instead of bringing out the outline.
